result.title: EgoHandWAM: Probing the Role of Hand Motion in Egocentric World Action Modeling
result.summary: How much does hand motion tell us about what a first-person camera will see next? EgoHandWAM forecasts three-dimensional wrist and fingertip trajectories and a future visual feature from the current image and recent hand states. We train on 751,065 EgoDex windows using a frozen DINOv2 encoder. On held-out development sessions, the action-only model reduces two-second wrist endpoint error from 60.26 to 56.48~mm relative to a stationary forecast. It still underestimates long reaches. Adding future-feature supervision gives nearly identical trajectory accuracy. With the recorded hand history, the visual head reduces smooth L1 error by 1.32\% relative to copying the current feature. Shuffling histories across sessions erases this gain. In a separate four-task probe, adding recorded future displacements to observed context and future tracking-validity masks reduces visual-feature error by 3.93\%. Masks alone give little improvement. A trajectory predicted from the same observations adds little. On two simulated RoboTwin tasks, substituting aligned human examples for an auxiliary batch of robot examples gives no consistent increase in task success across three training seeds.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作从当前图像与近期手部状态预测三维腕部/指尖轨迹及未来 DINOv2 视觉特征，在 EgoDex 大规模窗口上训练，并通过打乱手部历史、掩码消融等探针检验手部运动信息对未来视觉预测的实际贡献。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预测未来视觉特征＋条件信息消融」的设置可供核查 LVR 中隐状态是否真正吸收特定证据（如打乱历史即抹去增益这类因果式检验），但任务为自中心世界建模，与推理期 latent 状态的关系需进一步确认。
